Series::strides¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

pluss::msharp::RangeView::Int Series::strides() const

Read The Complete Storage Walk¶

strides() returns one element-stride per axis. If coordinate i[d] advances by one, the storage offset advances by strides()[d] elements. Combined with sizes(), this metadata describes the Series view without copying its payload.

The returned RangeView borrows metadata from the Series implementation. It is cheap and read-only; do not retain it beyond the lifetime of the Series whose layout it describes. Use stride(dim) for one normalized axis, and strides() when inspecting or forwarding the complete layout.

Strides are measured in elements, not bytes. Multiply by dtype().itemsize when a byte distance is required. A zero stride denotes broadcasting: several logical coordinates read the same physical element. A larger-than-packed stride denotes holes, as in stepped or column slices. Neither property alone makes a view invalid.

Examples¶

1. Packed And Transposed Layouts¶

auto table = pluss::make_series({
    {4.0, 1.0, 4.0, 2.0},
    {3.0, 5.0, 0.0, 5.0},
});
auto print = [](const pluss::Series& x) {
  std::cout << "[";
  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < x.strides().size(); ++i) {
    if (i) std::cout << ",";
    std::cout << x.strides()[i];
  }
  std::cout << "]";
};
print(table);
std::cout << "\n";
print(table.transpose(0, 1));

Output¶

[4,1]
[1,4]

Transpose swaps shape and stride metadata; it does not rearrange storage.

2. Broadcasting Introduces A Zero Stride¶

auto wide = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 3.0})
                .unsqueeze(0)
                .expand({4, 3});
std::cout << "strides=";
print(wide);

Output¶

strides=[0,1]

Advancing through the four logical rows does not advance storage.

3. Scalars Have No Axis Metadata¶

std::cout << "strides=";
print(pluss::make_series(1.0));

Output¶

strides=[]

4. A Column Split Can Be Non-Dense Without Overlap¶

auto first_column = table.split_with_sizes({1, 3}, 1)[0];
std::cout << first_column << "\nstrides=";
print(first_column);

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[2,1], strides=[4,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=false)
data=[[4],
  [3]]
strides=[4,1]

The two values are four storage elements apart. The view is valid and non-overlapping, but not dense.

strides() does not allocate or participate in reverse mode. Calling it on an undefined Series is invalid because there is no metadata to borrow.
